help.title: How to use
help.b1: Pick a board size in the top bar. Changing the board clears what is on it.
help.b2: Drag an accessory from the left panel onto the board. It snaps to the nearest slot that fits.
help.b3: A green ghost means it will drop there; red means something is in the way.
help.b4: Click a placed item to select it, then drag to move it or press Delete to remove it.
help.b5: Hardware and multi-item sets cannot be placed on the board — add them with + in the left panel and they still count toward the total.
help.s1: R — rotate the item you are dragging, or the selected one, a quarter turn
help.s2: Delete or Backspace — remove the selected item
help.s3: Left drag on empty space — orbit the camera
help.s5: Reset view — return the camera to straight-on
help.p1: Language and price market are separate. Switching language never changes the prices.
help.p2: Uncheck anything you already own to price only the upgrade.
help.p3: Some items are sold in multipacks. The Buy column shows packs to order, not pieces.
help.p4: Click any price to type your own — useful for second-hand parts or a market we cannot fetch.
help.p5: Choose Custom prices to enter everything yourself in any currency.
help.n1: The 40 mm slot grid is measured from IKEA product photos, so hole counts match the real boards.
help.n2: Peg spacing is estimated — IKEA does not publish it — so an accessory may sit slightly off.
help.n3: An item may overhang the board edge. Only its pegs must land in real slots.
help.s6: Ctrl/Cmd + Z — undo · Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Z — redo
help.s7: Share link — copies a link containing your whole configuration
help.b6: Custom parts: define your own rounded-box placeholders. They are never priced and never travel in a share link.
help.b7: A board you define yourself gets a ⟳ button to hang it the other way round — 36×56 becomes 56×36. Like changing the size, this clears that board. IKEA's own boards have no ⟳: see Good to know.
help.n4: SKÅDIS slots are upright ovals, and an accessory hooks by dropping into one — so an IKEA board only hangs one way up and there is no turn button on it. A board you define yourself can be turned; if you gave it upright slots, the same limit applies to it.
help.pv1: No cookies, no accounts, and no profile of you. The one thing measured is that a visit happened, counted by counter.dev — which sees your country, the site you came from, your screen size and your browser language, and never links page views to a person.
help.pv1off: No analytics, no cookies, no accounts. Nothing you do here is sent to us, because there is no server — the whole app runs in your browser.
help.pv2: Your wall, prices and preferences are saved in this browser’s local storage and stay on this device. Clearing site data erases them.
help.pv3: Prices come from a snapshot built into the page. Only if you press Refresh prices does your browser contact IKEA directly, which shows them your IP address like visiting ikea.com would.
help.pv4: Your wall itself is never sent anywhere. If you would rather not be counted at all, untick the box below — the choice is remembered in this browser and applies from your next visit onwards.
help.a1: Free and open source, under the MIT licence.
help.a2: Source, issues and contributions on GitHub ↗
help.b8: On a touch screen, tap a placed item to select it — arrows, rotate and delete appear over the 3D view.
help.s8: Arrow keys — move the selected item one hole at a time
help.b9: Tap + beside any accessory to drop it on the board without dragging, then move it with the arrows.
help.b10: Allow items to overlap lets you move something past its neighbours. Pegs still have to land in real slots, and it is never carried in a share link.
help.b11: Click a board’s name to rename it — “Garage”, “Over the bench”. Names stay in this browser and never travel in a share link.
help.b12: Colours in the top bar repaints the 3D view. Switching theme puts those colours back to the theme’s own.
help.p6: Click any count to change it. Setting it below what is on the board says you already own some — the wall is untouched, only the price drops.
help.b13: Define custom board describes a pegboard that is not SKÅDIS — one you printed, a sheet of 1-inch hardboard, a metal panel. Set its size in holes, the spacing, the hole shape and the thickness.
help.n5: A custom board with spacing other than 40 mm will hold accessories on screen, but SKÅDIS hooks are built for 40 mm centres and will not physically fit it.
help.n6: Custom boards are never priced — they have no article number. Their geometry does travel in a share link, so the wall you send is the wall the other person sees.
help.b14: A custom part uses SKÅDIS pegs unless you switch it to Self-defined, which opens the spacing, layout, shape, size and length. The dialog says so if the pegs match nothing on your wall. It also reopens with the last size and pegs you entered, until the page is reloaded.
help.n7: Custom boards travel in a share link; custom parts do not. Send a link and the other person sees your panels, but any placeholder bodies on them are left out, and the app tells you how many.
